Thanks again for the demo earlier this week — the team is excited about the latency improvements. We ran a quick usage check and have about 9 unused evaluation days left on our current time-boxed run (we started 10/22). Before we escalate to procurement, two asks:

Hi Samir — appreciate the note. Short answers up front, then a recommendation:

- Yes, we can map leftover evaluation time into a one-time SKU top-up (we call this a "graceband" addendum) which shows up as an invoiceable SKU for procurement.
- For first-year committed packages tied to that SKU we typically offer a 10–20% discount depending on annual commit size and billing cadence; I outlined two options below.

Recommendation (fastest path):
- Sign a 30-day graceband addendum that converts the unused days into a SKU credit bucket (visible on PO). After PO, we convert to a committed 12-month rate with a 12% introductory discount if they sign the annual commitment within 30 days. This avoids an immediate contract amendment and lets procurement get a PO out quickly.

Pricing options (high-level):
- Option A — SKU top-up (one-time): 9 days -> 450,000 token-equivalent SKU (one invoice). List price $7,250. Suggested offer: $6,380 (12% off).
- Option B — SKU + 12-month commit: apply SKU as a credit toward a reserved capacity monthly plan. Example: 12-month commit $75,000 -> effective 12% intro discount first-year, SKU applied to first invoice.

Next steps I can take this morning: attach a short one-page addendum and a tidy PO-friendly SKU line. Marcus, can you confirm the throughput mapping and whether the SKU conversion needs an engineering caveat?

If that works, Samir — I can send the addendum as an Excel SKU line for procurement to slot into the PO.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

Olga / Samir — quick technical confirmation:

- The 9 unused days map to an approximate KV-cache warm-start cost and token throughput we estimate as ~450,000 token-equivalent units based on Integro's telemetry (see attached report). The SKU we propose is a token-equivalent bucket, not reserved GPU-hours — that avoids infra reconfiguration.
- No engineering caveat needed for the addendum; we simply provision a token bucket tied to their account and it will be applied at invoice time.

If procurement insists on a GPU-hour SKU, we can translate to an hourly equivalent but pricing will be different and slower to approve.

-Marcus
